title.why: Tracker heading 'SB 1297: The Conversational AI Safety Act'.

date_published.why: 'Enacted March 31, 2026'; this is the enactment date, which the register uses for enacted laws.

date_in_force.why: 'Effective July 1, 2027'. Other web results agree except one that gives 2026; all rest on unstored pages.

status.why: Enacted 31 March 2026 with effect on 1 July 2027, which is after today (14 Oct 2026); 'Adopted, not yet in force' is correct.

issuing_body.why: 'signed by Governor Brad Little' is not in the stored tracker (extractor says so). The Idaho Legislature as issuer is reasonable but unstored.

official_identifier.why: 'S 1297 (2026 Regular Session, 68th Idaho Legislature)': bill number supported ('SB 1297'), '68th Idaho Legislature' is not in the stored tracker.

summary.why: Several claims are absent from the only stored source: Attorney General enforcement, the USD 1,000 and USD 500,000 penalties, the three-hour disclaimer, referral to crisis services, no claim of licensed mental-health care, and 'where the operator knows a user is a minor'. The penalty sentence also uses the hedge 'reported' (AGENTS.md rule 5).

notes.why: Senate 21-12 and House 54-12 votes, '19 Mar 2026' and the 'already in effect' commentary are not in the stored tracker; 'Reported', 'Trackers give' and 'the enrolled text should be checked' are hedges or process language. The Nebraska comparison is partly visible (similar title), but the 1 Jul 2027 Nebraska date is not checked in the stored text.

verification.note.why: Accurately lists what the stored tracker confirms and what it does not; CAUTION present.

summary_claims.claim: Operators must show a disclaimer repeated at least every three hours
The Attorney General enforces; penalties USD 1,000 per violation capped at USD 500,000
Operators may not use reward features to engage minors and must block sexually explicit content for minors

scope.note: State law on conversational AI and minors' safety; in scope as a sub-national AI-specific law.

note: Title, enactment date, effective date, status and legal force are supported by the Transparency Coalition tracker (level C). The summary and notes go well beyond that one stored source: AG enforcement, penalties, the three-hour disclaimer, the votes and the Governor's signature are unstored, and both texts contain hedges ('reported', 'Trackers give', 'should be checked'). A targeted search found no newer version; it did show LegiScan listing Session Law Chapter 249 and mostly July 1, 2027, but those pages are not stored. A human should decide whether to trim the summary to the stored text or store a bill copy.
